note: The dependency catalogue and the hand-authored half of the deferred-knowledge registry. Deferred rule cards are NOT listed here -- they are derived from the store at report time, so a card cannot be inert without appearing in the backlog. See Rules/tools/backlog.py.

dep.lord-of-house.title: lord_of_house extractor
dep.lord-of-house.detail: Which graha rules which house, given the lagna. Needs the sign-lordship table from Phaladeepika ch. 1 v. 6, which is itself deferred.
dep.lord-of-house.effort_basis: read a lordship table out of rule cards and emit one fact per house

dep.aspects.title: aspect engine
dep.aspects.detail: Graha drishti, including the special aspects of Mars, Jupiter and Saturn.
dep.aspects.effort_basis: quarter/half/three-quarter/full glance plus the special aspects

dep.conjunct.title: conjunction extractor
dep.conjunct.detail: Two grahas in the same sign or within an orb; the classics mean the same bhava.

dep.hemmed-between.title: hemming (papakartari / subhakartari) extractor
dep.hemmed-between.detail: A graha or house flanked by malefics or benefics in the 2nd and 12th from it. The mechanism is cheap now that dep.nature and dep.graha-frame exist, but the *definition* is doctrine and it is printed in chapter 6 ("When the 12th and 2nd from the Lagna are occupied by benefics, the Yoga so formed is called Subhakartari"), which is not encoded. Writing the two offsets into Engine/facts.py would be the engine supplying doctrine, so the predicate waits on that chapter rather than on the code.
dep.hemmed-between.effort_basis: occupants of the 2nd and 12th from a graha; blocked on the chapter that defines which houses those are, not on the arithmetic

dep.dignity.title: dignity extractor
dep.dignity.detail: Exaltation, fall, deep exaltation and fall, own sign and Moolatrikona, all read from Phaladeepika ch. 1 vv. 6-7 reference cards. The friendly / neutral / inimical half is NOT included -- see dep.dignity-friendship.
dep.dignity.effort_basis: exaltation/fall/Moolatrikona from ch.1, friendship from ch.2

dep.combust.title: combustion extractor
dep.combust.detail: Asta -- proximity to the Sun within the per-graha orb.
dep.combust.effort_basis: per-graha orbs; the orb values are doctrine and their source is not yet located

dep.vargottama.title: vargottama extractor
dep.vargottama.detail: Same sign in D-1 and D-9. Blocked on the varga engine.
dep.vargottama.effort_basis: D-1/D-9 sign equality once vargas exist

dep.varga.title: varga (divisional chart) engine
dep.varga.detail: D-9 at minimum; the MVP scope names D-1, D-3 and D-9.
dep.varga.effort_basis: divisional longitude arithmetic plus a second frame in the ChartBundle

dep.nature.title: benefic/malefic classification
dep.nature.detail: Natural and temporal benefic/malefic status of each graha. Doctrine, not arithmetic -- it must come from rule cards, and the chapters that state it are deferred.
dep.nature.effort_basis: benefic/malefic, including the conditional cases for Mercury and the Moon

dep.nature-occupancy.title: occupancy of a house by grahas of a given nature
dep.nature-occupancy.detail: "Malefics in the 12th, 4th and 8th" -- a quantified statement over the occupants of a named house. Needs both dep.nature and quantification over occupants.
dep.nature-occupancy.effort_basis: quantification over the occupants of a named house

dep.occupant-count.title: occupant counting
dep.occupant-count.detail: "As many women as the number of planets in the 7th." The claim is a count, not a category, and neither the condition language nor the claim schema can express one. Delivered as two predicates: occupant_count(house, n) and conjunct_count(graha, n). The count is bound by a variable rather than compared against, so a card can learn a number and report it without any arithmetic entering the condition language.
dep.occupant-count.effort_basis: counts as claims -- the claim schema has no numeric form

dep.strength.title: planetary and house strength (Stage 4)
dep.strength.detail: Shadbala and bhava bala. Sourceable from Phaladeepika ch. 4, which is deferred.
dep.strength.effort_basis: shadbala is six components, each its own calculation

dep.dasa.title: vimshottari dasa engine
dep.dasa.detail: Dasa and antardasa periods. Sourceable from Phaladeepika ch. 19.
dep.dasa.effort_basis: vimshottari balance at birth plus a timeline, and claims that carry a window

dep.transit.title: transit (gochara) calculation
dep.transit.detail: Positions at a date other than birth, and the machinery to state a claim about a future window.
dep.transit.effort_basis: positions at a second instant and claims about a future window

dep.ashtakavarga.title: ashtakavarga
dep.ashtakavarga.detail: Bhinnashtakavarga and sarvashtakavarga. Sourceable from Phaladeepika ch. 23-24.
dep.ashtakavarga.effort_basis: bhinna and sarva construction with the 337 invariant

dep.sign-class.title: sign classification
dep.sign-class.detail: Odd/even, movable/fixed/dual, and the rest. Reference doctrine from Phaladeepika ch. 1, deferred.
dep.sign-class.effort_basis: a classification table read from cards

dep.house-class.title: house classification
dep.house-class.detail: Kendra, trikona, upachaya, dusthana. Reference doctrine from Phaladeepika ch. 1, deferred.
dep.house-class.effort_basis: a classification table read from cards

dep.graha-class.title: graha classification
dep.graha-class.detail: Male/female/hermaphrodite and similar categories. Reference doctrine from Phaladeepika ch. 2, deferred.
dep.graha-class.effort_basis: a classification table read from cards

dep.condition-variables.title: variables in the condition language
dep.condition-variables.detail: Named variables (`?g`) that bind the same value across the leaves of one condition, existential quantification over the grahas the FactSet contains, and negation as failure over a subexpression whose variables stay local. Deliberately not an expression language: no arithmetic, no comparison, and no binding to anything the chart did not produce. A quantified card yields one claim per satisfying binding, so the report names the graha instead of saying 'some planet'.
dep.condition-variables.effort_basis: condition language, evaluator, binding trace, and Stage 9 re-evaluation

dep.multi-span-quote.title: quotation across two spans
dep.multi-span-quote.detail: A card carries one contiguous char_span. Where a governing sentence states the effect for several dispositions printed as separate paragraphs, no single span holds both.
dep.multi-span-quote.effort_basis: card schema, build tool, verifier and renderer all assume one span

dep.moon-frame.title: the Moon as an alternative reference frame
dep.moon-frame.detail: "From the lagna or the Moon." Chandra-lagna is named out of scope for the MVP. Satisfied by dep.graha-frame: in_house_from(graha, Moon, house) counts houses from the Moon, the Moon being one graha among the reference bodies.
dep.moon-frame.effort_basis: the Moon as a second reference frame

dep.graha-frame.title: houses counted from a graha
dep.graha-frame.detail: "The 7th from Venus and the Moon." Requires a per-graha house frame, not just the lagna and the Moon.
dep.graha-frame.effort_basis: houses counted from a graha rather than the lagna

dep.dignity-override.title: dignity-override mechanism
dep.dignity-override.detail: A rule that changes the dignity another rule is keyed on, rather than asserting anything itself. Retrogression and vargottama both do this.
dep.dignity-override.effort_basis: a rule that rewrites the dignity another rule is keyed on

dep.rule-transfer.title: rule-transfer mechanism
dep.rule-transfer.detail: A rule that asserts another rule's claim under a different condition, without restating it. Resolved by letting the meta card fire as its own quantified claim (an ordinary use of dep.condition-variables) rather than by expanding it into cards for each rule it refers to, which would restate them.
dep.rule-transfer.effort_basis: a card that asserts another card's claim under a different condition

dep.native-sex.title: the native's sex in the birth record
dep.native-sex.detail: Several rules differ only by the sex of the native. BirthRecord does not carry it, so the engine cannot tell which of a pair applies.
dep.native-sex.effort_basis: one field on BirthRecord and a scope test in activation

dep.second-nativity.title: a second nativity
dep.second-nativity.detail: Rules that read the spouse's chart alongside the native's. The pipeline handles one chart.
dep.second-nativity.effort_basis: a second chart through the whole pipeline

dep.adjudication.title: Stage 7 adjudication
dep.adjudication.detail: Conflict resolution, weighting and precedence between rules that disagree.

dep.manual-verification.title: human verification of the encoding
dep.manual-verification.detail: Cards are machine-checked against the corpus but no human has signed off on the reading of the rule. Every card's extraction.verified_by is still null.
dep.manual-verification.effort_basis: human reading of every card against its verse; scales with the store

dep.none.title: no dependency -- simply not yet done
dep.none.detail: Deferred by ordering, not by any missing capability. Available to encode now.

dep.upagraha.title: upagraha computation
dep.upagraha.detail: Gulika, Mandi and the other sub-planets. Sourceable from Phaladeepika ch. 25.

dep.prashna.title: prashna (horary) branch
dep.prashna.detail: Rules that read the chart of the moment a question is asked rather than a nativity. Their conditions are ordinary placements and would fire on a birth chart, so they must be held apart by branch, not by condition.
dep.prashna.effort_basis: a second chart source and a branch tag Stage 6 honours

dep.dignity-friendship.title: natural friendship (the unresolved half of dignity)
dep.dignity-friendship.detail: Whether a graha sits in a friend's, neutral's or enemy's sign, read from the graha's own row in the natural-friendship table against the lord of its sign. Both tables that carry it (the seven classical grahas, and Rahu/Ketu separately) are encoded and verified against the printed page -- the original 'the scan interleaved past reconstruction' diagnosis was wrong; the source is a clean pdf_text extraction, not a damaged scan.
dep.dignity-friendship.effort_basis: a table read from cards, once a human has checked the printed page -- done for the table itself (2026-08-19) and for the three cards this unlocks (below), not for the whole store

dep.correlated-negation.title: negation correlated with the current binding
dep.correlated-negation.detail: "Benefics in the 7th will produce good effects unless they happen to be lords of the 6th, 8th or 12th." The exclusion is about the graha that satisfied the first clause. Evaluated without the current binding, the negation asks whether anything at all is lord of the 8th -- true of every chart -- so the rule could never fire. Conjunctions now bind left to right and each child is solved under its predecessors' assignment.
dep.correlated-negation.effort_basis: threading the assignment through condition evaluation

dep.yoga-combination-count.title: counting how many sibling yoga-conditions are simultaneously true
dep.yoga-combination-count.detail: Several yoga verses grade their effect by how many related yoga-conditions a chart satisfies at once (Phaladeepika 6, closing the Pancha Mahapurusha cluster: one such yoga is merely fortunate, five make a person superior to an Emperor). The condition language can quantify over grahas and signs but has no way to ask how many sibling cards, or sibling condition-branches, are true together for one chart.
dep.yoga-combination-count.effort_basis: a way to count satisfied sibling conditions across a named group of cards

entries.reason: Rule-dense and encodable now; deferred by ordering only. Presentation of death-related material is governed by the sensitive-content policy and needs sign-off before any of it can reach a reader.

entries.reason: Rule-dense and encodable now; deferred by ordering only. Feeds Stage 7 weighting.

entries.reason: Encodable now; every card would be inert until dep.conjunct exists.

entries.reason: Encodable now; every card would be inert until both dep.dasa and dep.lord-of-house exist.

entries.locus: whole chapter - Effects of Ashtakavarga according to Horasara
entries.what: a second authority's ashtakavarga effects
entries.reason: Encodable now; inert until dep.ashtakavarga exists. Attributed to a different authority than ch. 23, so the two must stand independently.

entries.what: upagraha computation and effects
entries.reason: Encodable now; inert until the upagrahas are computed.

entries.reason: Encodable now; every card would be inert until dep.transit exists.

entries.what: sanyasa yogas
entries.reason: Rule-dense and encodable now; deferred by ordering only.

entries.what: the author's colophon and closing remarks
entries.reason: Narrative, not doctrine. Will be reviewed once for any rule hidden in the closing remarks, then written off.

entries.what: the translator's qualification of the Sun in the 10th: the good effects hold only for eight of the twelve lagnas
entries.reason: Tier-2 commentary that narrows a tier-1 card already in the store (PD.08.Sun.10). It is an exclusion on an existing rule, and the card schema records exclusions as prose only - nothing evaluates them.

entries.what: Manglik Dosha: Mars in the 7th, its effect by sex of the native, and the belief that it cancels when both partners are Manglik
entries.reason: Substantial tier-2 doctrine, deferred rather than skipped. It is scoped by the native's sex, states a cancellation rule the engine cannot express, and reads a second nativity.

entries.what: the translator arguing from aspects: the Sun in the 8th aspecting the 2nd, and why Jupiter in the lagna outranks Venus there
entries.reason: Tier-2 commentary whose reasoning is entirely about aspects. Encodable as a claim only once aspects are computed; until then a card would quote an argument the engine cannot follow.

entries.what: the translator on Saturn in the lagna (citing Brihat Jataka) and on Saturn in the 9th
entries.reason: Tier-2 commentary. The first quotes a second book from inside this one - it must be encoded as Phaladeepika reporting Brihat Jataka, not as a Brihat Jataka card, and that attribution has no representation in the card schema.

entries.what: a transcribed horoscope of Swami Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and its lagna note
entries.reason: Tier-3 apparatus: a worked example, not a rule. Recorded as deliberately excluded, not pending.

entries.what: the Bhava-Madhya proximity rule, and the doctrine that Rahu gives effects like Saturn and Ketu like Mars (Shani-vat Rahu, Kuja-vat Ketu)
entries.reason: Real doctrine, and the reason it is still unencoded: verse 34 with its worked examples and verse 35 appear to state opposite relationships between proximity to the Bhava-Madhya and strength of effect. Both must be encoded and the disagreement preserved, which needs adjudication. Para 132 also runs across a page break mid-sentence.

entries.what: a general caution that these effects are modified by lordship, aspect, conjunction and dignity, and a pointer to another book
entries.reason: The caution is method guidance rather than a rule with a condition; the pointer is a publisher's advertisement. Both written off as tier-3 apparatus.

entries.what: the chapter's closing formula
entries.reason: Colophon. Not doctrine.

entries.what: two transcribed horoscopes, their lagna notes, a worked example and an aside on Abraham Lincoln
entries.reason: Tier-3 apparatus: worked examples, not rules. Recorded as deliberately excluded, not pending.

entries.what: the chapter's closing formula
entries.reason: Colophon. Not doctrine.

entries.what: human sign-off that each card reads its verse correctly
entries.reason: Every card is machine-checked byte-exact against the corpus, but extraction.verified_by is null on all but four of them: PD.02.Friendship.NaturalTable (the table itself) and the three cards its extractor unlocked -- PD.09.Dignity.Friend, PD.09.Dignity.Neutral, PD.10.WifeDeprived.Lord7Afflicted -- each individually checked against its own verse, not signed off as a block. The machine can prove a card quotes the book faithfully; it cannot prove the condition encodes what the verse means.

entries.what: the invocation of the Sun and the author's obeisance to Saraswati, his deities and preceptors
entries.reason: Devotional invocation. It states no rule and conditions nothing, and encoding it as a card would put a benediction in the report as though a chart had activated it.

entries.what: the instruction to establish the birth time in Ghatikas by gnomon or instrument, and to compute the longitudes before judging anything
entries.reason: Method, not doctrine: it governs how a chart is erected rather than what any placement means. The engine already does what it asks, by a different instrument. Worth revisiting if birth-time precision is ever sourced to the classics rather than declared by the user.

entries.what: the column headings of the deep-exaltation table
entries.reason: Table furniture. The seven rows beneath it are encoded as PD.01.DeepExaltation.*, each quoting the sentence that introduces the table; the bare column headings add nothing a card could carry.

entries.what: a bracketed editorial sentence introducing the house-name lists
entries.reason: Printed in square brackets, which in this edition marks the translator's insertion rather than Mantreswara's text. It introduces the twelve lists that follow, all of which are encoded.

entries.what: the chapter's closing formula
entries.reason: Colophon. Not doctrine.

entries.what: the editorial paragraph introducing what the chapter is for
entries.reason: Framing rather than doctrine. The one principle it states -- that a house's subject is read from its lord -- is encoded separately as PD.02.Principle.LordCarriesSignification.

entries.what: a worked example in which a marriage occurred in the Dasa of Venus rather than the Dasa of the 7th lord, as some astrologers had predicted
entries.reason: Tier-3 apparatus: a case report, not a rule. It argues that the karaka can outweigh the house lord, which is a real claim, but it is made by example rather than stated as doctrine and would need adjudication to encode.

entries.what: the chapter's closing formula
entries.reason: Colophon. Not doctrine.

entries.what: whether the retrograde-as-exalted override extends to Rahu and Ketu
entries.reason: The verse says 'a planet' without exclusion, and the engine's own retrograde predicate already marks the nodes retrograde on every chart (their motion is always backward, by convention rather than vakri). Classical vakri doctrine is usually stated only for the five graha capable of direct and retrograde motion, and the nodes carry their own separate, disputed exaltation doctrine (see PD.01.Exaltation.RahuKetu.* -- three contradictory authorities, none singular). The override mechanism is gated on a singular exaltation card existing for the graha, which the nodes do not have, so it is silent for them today -- a consequence of what is encoded, not a decision that the verse excludes them. Recorded rather than decided so the question survives to be checked against the other books once a singular nodal exaltation card is encoded.

entries.what: the blanket condition that every yoga in the chapter needs strength in the Lagna/Moon and the yoga-forming planets
entries.reason: Applies to all named yogas in the chapter, not just the five Pancha Mahapurusha ones encoded in this slice. Recorded once here rather than duplicated per card; PD.06.Ruchaka, PD.06.Bhadra, PD.06.Hamsa, PD.06.Malavya and PD.06.Sasa each cross-reference this entry in their own note rather than repeating it. Untestable until dep.strength exists.

entries.what: the translator's introduction to the illustrative birth charts that follow
entries.reason: Tier-3 apparatus: framing for the worked examples, not a rule. Recorded as deliberately excluded, not pending.

entries.what: Stalin's horoscope, illustrating Ruchaka and Malavya Yogas
entries.reason: Tier-3 apparatus: a worked example, not a rule. Recorded as deliberately excluded, not pending.

entries.locus: p.56-57 (unnumbered, closing the Pancha Mahapurusha cluster)
entries.what: the five Mahapurusha yogas also count from the Moon, and compound in effect when more than one is present at once
entries.reason: Two claims neither of the five yoga cards test. First, 'identical with a kendra' in verses 1-5 is read from the lagna only in this slice; this closing sentence says the same combination counts equally from the Moon, which is expressible with the existing graha-frame machinery but was not attempted here -- the slice stays to the verses' own wording rather than silently widening it. Second, the graduated effect for holding two, three, four or all five yogas at once needs a way to count how many sibling cards are simultaneously satisfied, which the condition language cannot do today (dep.yoga-combination-count). Neither is built speculatively.

entries.what: Dr. Radhakrishnan's horoscope, illustrating a Pancha Mahapurusha combination
entries.reason: Tier-3 apparatus: a worked example, not a rule. Recorded as deliberately excluded, not pending.

entries.what: Moti Lal Nehru's horoscope, illustrating Hamsa Yoga
entries.reason: Tier-3 apparatus: a worked example, not a rule. Recorded as deliberately excluded, not pending.

entries.what: Sunapha, Anapha, Durudhara and Kemadruma Yogas
entries.reason: Not yet encoded; deferred by ordering, planned for a later chapter-6 slice. Verse 5 itself carries a hedged alternate Kemadruma reading ("some learned are of the opinion"), and the Notes add two more: Saravali's version and Hora Sara's version. A worked-example horoscope (Sardar Patel) is embedded and will be tier-3 apparatus when this slice is authored.

entries.what: Subhavesi, Subhavasi, Ubhayachari, Subhakartari, Papakartari and Susubha Yogas
entries.reason: Not yet encoded; deferred by ordering. Verse 8 (benefic-only) is explicitly contested by an unnamed "authoritative works" reading (any of five named grahas, regardless of nature) in the Notes, with the translator stating an editorial preference for Mantreswara's reading that must not be used to silently pick one. Saravali's Notes further give per-graha effects for Vesi and Vasi yogas, attributed doctrine from a second book. Verse 13 cross-references "the same as Sunapha and other yogas" -- a rule-transfer candidate (dep.rule-transfer, already implemented) for the later slice.

entries.what: Amala, Mahabhagya, Kesari, Sakata, Adhama/Sama/Varishtha, Vasumati, Pushkala, Sub(h)amala, Lakshmi, Gouri and Saraswati Yogas
entries.reason: Not yet encoded; deferred by ordering. Mahabhagya Yoga (v.14) is sex-scoped (dep.native-sex, already implemented) and carries a translator's note that Indira Gandhi's chart matched every effect but one, attributed to "other adverse planetary dispositions" rather than treated as a counterexample. Four illustrative horoscopes are embedded and will be tier-3 apparatus.

entries.what: Srikantha, Srinatha and Virinchi Yogas; the Parivartana (Maha/Dainya/Kahala) house-exchange family
entries.reason: Not yet encoded; deferred by ordering. The Parivartana pair enumeration (vv. 32-34 Notes) is confirmed genuinely defective in the printed book -- verified by rendering PDF pages 67-69 directly rather than trusting the flattened extraction -- item 18 of the 28-item Maha list is missing, items 17 and 20 are each printed twice with mismatched content, and item 13 of the 30-item Dainya list is truncated. Whether to transcribe only the legible items or derive the complete set from verse 32's own combinatorics is an editorial decision for that slice, not resolved here. A translator's Note (paras 140-144) also reports Uttarakalamrita's directly contradicting reading of the same 6th/8th/12th-lord exchange (auspicious under three extra conditions, "quite reverse" of Phaladeepika's own Dainya) -- a contradicts pair for that slice. An Indira Gandhi worked example is embedded and will be tier-3 apparatus.

entries.what: A second, unrelated Kahala Yoga (a dispositor-chain test) and Parvata Yoga
entries.reason: Not yet encoded; deferred by ordering. This Kahala Yoga (v.35) shares its name with the house-exchange Kahala Yoga of v.32 but tests an entirely different combination -- the two must never be conflated when this slice is authored. Two worked-example horoscopes are embedded and will be tier-3 apparatus.

entries.what: Raja Yoga, Shankha Yoga, and the seven planets-in-N-signs family (Vallaki/Veena, Dharma, Hasha, Kendra, Shula, Yuga, Gola)
entries.reason: Not yet encoded. The seven planets-in-N-signs family needs one new engine fact -- a count of how many distinct signs the seven classical grahas (excluding the nodes) occupy between them -- which nothing in the current vocabulary computes; occupant_count counts occupants of one house, not signs occupied overall. Not built speculatively; Raja and Shankha Yoga need nothing new and could be encoded independently of it.

entries.what: Adhiyoga
entries.reason: Not yet encoded; deferred by ordering. A Notes aside attributed to "Shruti Kirti ... according to Vyas" disputes how strictly the three yoga-forming grahas must be distributed across the three houses -- a contradicts pair for that slice. A Sardar Patel worked example is embedded and will be tier-3 apparatus.

entries.what: Twelve yogas keyed to the 6th/8th/12th lords occupying a dusthana (Ava, Nisswa, Mriti, Kuhu, Pamara, Harsha, Dushkriti, Sarala, Nirbhagya, Duryoga [10th house], Daridrya, Vimala)
entries.reason: Not yet encoded; deferred by ordering. The richest single contradiction in the chapter: Mantreswara calls Harsha/Sarala/Vimala auspicious, Parashara's own nine-combination breakdown (quoted in full, paras 220-228) rates most of the same placements negatively, and Dr. B.V. Raman is quoted at length disputing the premise entirely, with the translator noting these three yogas appear in none of Brihat Jataka, Saravali or Jataka Parijata. "Duryoga" here (the 10th-house member) shares its name with the unrelated weak/strong-lord Duryoga of verse 70 and must stay distinguishable.

entries.what: A second, unrelated Duryoga (weak/strong 6th-8th-12th vs. 1st-4th-9th-10th lord test) and the chapter's closing formula
entries.reason: Verse 70 needs dep.strength directly ("vested with strength" / "weak or combust" gates both halves of the test) and is not testable until it exists. The colophon ("Thus ends the sixth chapter...") is narrative, not doctrine, matching every other chapter's closing formula.
